info.title: UniFi Access API reference (PDF, revision 2026-03-23): transcription by this project, not a vendor document

x-note: Written by hand from the cached PDF under the rules of docs/adr/0022-access-contract-transcription.md. Facts only: no vendor descriptions, examples or other prose. Checked against the PDF text by npm run api:reconcile.

x-declined.reason: Request header in every section; the transport sends the bearer token (ADR 0022 §6).

Typed Array[Object], but every sample (pp.18, 20) shows one object, and the text says a user has at most one Touch Pass. Either reading would fail reads that send the other; the Touch Pass reads of chapter 6 return the same data.
Typed Boolean, but its example is expand[]=access_policy: the row contradicts itself. §3.20 reads a user's access policies.
Typed Boolean, but its example is expand[]=access_policy: the row contradicts itself. §3.20 reads a user's access policies.
An array whose item type is not documented ("reserved for future use", always empty).
An array whose item type is not documented ("reserved for future use", always empty).
An object used as a map from user ID to email address. The translator accepts no typed map in a request (ADR 0018), and the PDF does not say whether it is needed beside ids.
An array whose item type is not documented ("reserved for future use", always empty).

get.x-note: page_num and page_size are typed String in the table, although the examples are numbers.

put.x-note: The curl sample targets /api/v1/developer/user and also sends pin_code. The method line and the field table win: pin_code is not accepted. status lists ACTIVE and DEACTIVATED as examples, not as the allowed set.
The curl sample uses DELETE; the method line says PUT.

get.x-note: The curl sample targets /api/v1/developer/developer/user_groups; the method line wins.

post.x-note: The body is a JSON array of user IDs, as the unlabelled row and the sample show.
The body is a JSON array of user IDs, as the unlabelled row and the sample show.

get.x-note: The response sample nests the list in an object ("data": { [ ... ] }), which is not valid JSON; it is read as a list of users, as in §3.5. user_id and status are typed String, so one value each is accepted although the examples repeat them. The sample shows no pagination.

put.x-note: No request body; the sample sends an empty one.
emails, a map from user ID to email address, is declined (see x-declined).
The body is a JSON array of plate numbers; the row is printed with the label "-".

post.x-note: A multipart upload; not generated until it is decided (ADR 0022 §5).

User.x-note: touch_pass is declined (see x-declined). avatar_relative_path, email and username appear only in the samples of the user group member reads (§3.18, §3.19) and the search (§3.24), which name this schema.

UserAccessPolicy.x-note: From the user read samples only; replaced by citations of the §5.1 table when chapter 5 is transcribed.

UserGroup.x-note: The PDF has no user group table; all fields come from samples.
